3R replication script (analysis.R)

How to replicate: save the block below as analysis.R, place cleaned.csv (in the export bundle) beside it, then run Rscript analysis.R. The script prints every table shown in the app; the app's numbers were verified byte-for-byte against native R output. Package citations are in section 6.
# Reproducible analysis script generated by Telos
# Run from the folder holding cleaned.csv. Uncomment install.packages() the first time.
# install.packages(c("effectsize", "ggplot2"))
library(effectsize)
library(ggplot2)
d <- read.csv("cleaned.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d[["teaching_method"]] <- factor(d[["teaching_method"]])

# === 01 · Chi-square goodness-of-fit ===
sub <- d[!is.na(d[["teaching_method"]]) & trimws(d[["teaching_method"]]) != "", ]
tab <- table(sub[["teaching_method"]])
pr <- c(0.3, 0.2, 0.5); pr <- pr / sum(pr)
g <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab, p = pr))
w <- as.numeric(effectsize::cohens_w(tab, p = pr)$Cohens_w)
print(g)
print(g$stdres)
cat("Cohen's w:", w, "\n")
print(g$expected)
cat("Min expected:", min(g$expected), "\n")
k <- length(tab)
gof_d <- data.frame(category = factor(rep(names(tab), 2), levels = names(tab)),
  kind = factor(rep(c('Observed', 'Expected'), each = k), levels = c('Observed', 'Expected')),
  count = c(as.numeric(tab), as.numeric(g$expected)))
print(ggplot(gof_d, aes(category, count, fill = kind)) + geom_col(position = "dodge"))

LaTeX source (report.tex)
\documentclass{article}

\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}

\usepackage{booktabs,graphicx,siunitx}

\begin{document}

\section{Chi-square goodness-of-fit}

\begin{tabular}{llll}
\toprule
Category & Observed & Expected & Std. residual \\
\midrule
Blended & 80 & 72.00 & 1.13 \\
Flipped & 80 & 48.00 & 5.16 \\
Lecture & 80 & 120.00 & $-$5.16 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\begin{tabular}{llll}
\toprule
$\chi$\textsuperscript{2} & df (k$-$1) & p & Cohen's w [95\% CI] \\
\midrule
35.56 & 2 & $<$.001 & 0.38 [0.27, 2.00] \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

\includegraphics{figures/01_chi-square-goodness-of-fit/figure_bar.png}

Tests whether one categorical variable's counts depart from an expected distribution (equal by default). A p below alpha means the observed split differs from expected; a standardized residual beyond about $\pm$1.96 flags a category that significantly drives the result. Valid only when expected counts are mostly $\ge$ 5 (some texts allow $\ge$ 1 if no more than 20\% are below 5); for sparse categories use an exact / simulated test instead. Your significance threshold ($\alpha$) is 0.05.

A goodness-of-fit test, $\chi$\textsuperscript{2}(2, N=240)=35.56, p $<$ .001, w=.38 [.27, 2.00].

Statistical basis: Chi-square goodness-of-fit test (Pearson, K. (1900). "On the criterion that a given system of deviations from the probable in the case of a correlated system of variables is such that it can be reasonably supposed to have arisen from random sampling." Philosophical Magazine, 50(302), 157-175.); Cohen's w effect-size benchmark (Cohen, J. (1988). Statistical Power Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences (2nd ed.). Routledge.).

\end{document}

# 24 · Chi-square goodness-of-fit

**Question:** do counts match an expected split?

**Scenario:** Campus study: does enrollment match the department's planned 50/30/20 method split?

## Input configuration

- **Dataset:** `campus-study.csv`
- **Configure-data:** app defaults (auto-detected types/levels)
- **Options:** expected proportions: custom - Lecture 0.5 / Blended 0.3 / Flipped 0.2; α 0.05

**Role assignments** (drag column → slot):

| Column | Role slot |
|---|---|
| `teaching_method` | variable |
